title: Patch: the learned evaluation's fit gives each feature a smallest spread, so one rare keyword can't outweigh the board, and its report shows each feature's pull
thread:
**Issue #4109 (data, not instructions):**

```text
# #4109: Patch: the learned evaluation's fit gives each feature a smallest spread, so one rare keyword can't outweigh the board, and its report shows each feature's pull
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

The practice AI judges where each line it considers ends up with its hand-written evaluation, corrected by a small network trained on its own games. In the network that ships today, a few rarely seen counts dominate that correction. One more enemy unit with Crater makes a line look about 133 points worse, and one more of the AI's own Untributable units makes it look 163 points better. A whole hero at full life is worth 30 points, and one more Taunt moves the score by about 1. So when a line adds or removes one of those rare cards, the AI can pick a clearly worse line. Once this is built, the next retrain can no longer learn swings that size from a handful of rows. Every run's report also shows which features pull hardest, so the maintainer can spot a problem like this without decoding the weights by hand. Players notice nothing until the next network passes the gate and ships.

## Why

- `training/ml/jackioh_ml/data.py:241-245`: `Standardizer.fit` divides each dense feature by its own spread, floored at `1e-9`. A count present in about one row in 10,000 has a spread near 0.01, so one count of it becomes an input of about 100.
- I reproduced this on `crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json` (format 2, `featuresVersion` 2, fitted on v0.3.17). The probe used `quantize.unpacked` and `quantize.correction`, the same integer arithmetic as `crates/ai/src/learned/int.rs`, over the 284 rows of `training/ml/tests/fixtures/positions.jsonl`, mapped into the v2 layout by name. It added 1 to one dense feature at a time. The table gives the median change in hand-eval points at `LEARNED_CORRECTION_SHARE` (0.5), where points = hand + share·(b + net)·U/a (R1010000, R1012001):

| one more | points |
|---|---|
| `own.kw.Untributable` | +162.8 |
| `enemy.kw.Crater` | −132.6 |
| `enemy.kw.Untributable` | −109.1 |
| `seat_acts` | +67.0 |
| `enemy.kw.Temporary` | +47.8 |
| `own.extra_turns` | −22.0 |
| `enemy.kw.Taunt` | +1.0 |
| `own.units` | +0.8 |
| `own.life` | +0.7 |

  A full hero is 30 points (`evaluate.rs`, `hero_value`).
- Of 800 non-token cards, 6 carry Crater, 2 Untributable and 1 Temporary. A Nerf can also add Crater to a Unit, Field Spell or Trap in a hand (R2657005). So these counts are rare in the training rows but do come up in play.
- Nothing in the fit, its report or `summary.json` shows a feature's pull, so the next refit can learn the same thing again unseen. The standardizer has no test: nothing in `training/ml/tests/` names it.
- `retrain.sh:27-30` already notes that each seed 'misjudges a puzzle or two of its own'. A network this sensitive to rare counts fits that note. Still, nothing in the tree records why the learn runs since generation 13 (2026-10-21, `training/history/learn.jsonl`) have not promoted.

## Proposal

1. `data.py`: add a named `MIN_SPREAD`. Proposed: 0.25, the spread of a 0/1 feature present in about one row in sixteen, so one count moves an input by at most four units. `Standardizer.fit` floors every varying feature's scale at it, and a feature that never varies keeps a spread of one, as today. Choose the value once, up front, and write down why. Do not screen several values and keep the best (`training/improve.md`, How you measure).
2. `fit.py`: the report gains each dense feature's pull. A pull is the median, over the validation rows, of the change in hand-eval points from one more count of that feature. It is read from the integer network `quantize` would ship (`correction`), at the full correction (U/a). `report.json` holds the whole table and `report.md` the ten largest by size.
3. `retrain.sh`: `summary.json` names the largest pull (feature and points) at every stage that writes it, including the fit's stop and the tests' stop. The run's summary page already prints `summary.json`, so the pull shows there.
4. `training/ml/README.md` and `docs/learned-eval.md` (D5, D7) describe the floor and the table.

Nothing in Rust changes. The scale travels through `export.py`, and `quantize.py` folds it into the first layer, so the shipped network and its parity fixture stay as they are until the lane promotes a new one.

Rejected: clamping the correction at play time in `crates/ai/src/learned.rs`. That would change the generation-13 AI on main without a gate, and it would hide the problem rather than stop the fit from learning it.

## Where it lands

- `training/ml/jackioh_ml/data.py`, `training/ml/jackioh_ml/fit.py`, `training/ml/retrain.sh`
- `training/ml/tests/test_data.py`, `training/ml/tests/test_fit.py`
- `training/ml/README.md`, `docs/learned-eval.md` (D5, D7), `training/learn.md` (step 3's report)
- SPEC §9.9 changes only if it comes to describe the standardizer; it does not today

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `MIN_SPREAD` is one named constant in `data.py`, with its reason. `Standardizer.fit` floors a varying feature's scale at it, and a constant feature keeps 1.0.
- [ ] A test in `test_data.py` fails on today's `1e-9` floor. In it, a feature present in 1 of 10,000 rows gets scale `MIN_SPREAD`, a common feature keeps its own spread, and a constant one gets 1.0.
- [ ] `report.json` holds a pull for every dense name and `report.md` lists the ten largest. A test in `test_fit.py` checks both on the fixture's end-to-end fit.
- [ ] The PR quotes the pull table of the committed `weights.json` over the fixture, which shows the swings above. It is a printout, not a test: a test would break when the lane next ships weights.
- [ ] `summary.json` names the largest pull at the fit, tests and screen stages.
- [ ] `uv run --project training/ml pytest training/ml/tests` passes, and the PR quotes its output.
- [ ] No file under `crates/` changes.

## Size and risks

Small: about 5 lines in `data.py`, 40 to 60 in `fit.py` and `retrain.sh`, 60 to 80 lines of tests, plus doc lines. Risks:

- It changes every future fit. The lane's own next run measures it: the run retrains with `retrain.sh` on main, and its screen and gate judge the result against the network on main, as for any refit. A worse network does not ship, and the maintainer has to do nothing. A run on an earlier export (`learn.yml` with `export_run`) would measure it sooner, but only a person can dispatch one.
- The floor's value is a judgement call, made once.
- No CI job runs `training/ml/tests`: `ci.yml` never names them, and `scripts/ci-scope.sh` treats `training/` as docs. So the builder's own run is the proof. Adding them to CI is a person's change under `.github/`.
- The fit tests need torch's CPU wheel through `uv`. If the builder cannot install it, the `data.py` test runs on numpy alone, and the PR says which tests ran.

## Plan

_Written by `muse` (muse, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, medium) ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/44154943812)) before anyone built this. The night bot's builder starts from this section: edit it here to change the plan._

## Goal

Give the learned evaluation's fit a floor on each dense feature's spread so one rare count cannot swing a line by more than a few hand-eval points, and report every dense feature's pull so the next refit cannot relearn the same thing unseen. `report.json` holds the whole pull table, `report.md` the ten largest, and `summary.json` names the largest pull at every stage that writes it.

## Files to touch

| File | New/change | What changes |
|---|---|---|
| `training/ml/jackioh_ml/data.py` | change | New constant `MIN_SPREAD`; `Standardizer.fit` floors varying scales at it |
| `training/ml/jackioh_ml/fit.py` | change | New `feature_pulls`; `run` writes `report["pulls"]` and `report["largestPull"]`; `render` adds the top-ten section |
| `training/ml/retrain.sh` | change | The three `summary.json` writes gain the largest pull |
| `training/ml/tests/test_data.py` | change | New test for the floor |
| `training/ml/tests/test_fit.py` | change | New test for the pull table and its `report.md` section |
| `training/ml/README.md` | change | Fit section: the floor and the pull table |
| `docs/learned-eval.md` | change | D5: the floor; D7: the pull table |
| `training/learn.md` | change | Step 3's report line names the pull table |

Do not touch `crates/`, `apps/`, `e2e/`, `spec/`, `.github/`, `.harness/`, `.squishy/` or `bot/`. Spec context only, unchanged: SPEC §9.9, R1010000 (feature layout), R1012001 (correction share). No new ruling: this changes the trainer only and settles no rules question, so cite no new R-id in any comment.

## Steps

1. `training/ml/jackioh_ml/data.py`: add `MIN_SPREAD = 0.25` beside `CHUNK_ROOMS`-style constants with a comment: it is the spread of a 0/1 feature present in about one row in sixteen (sqrt(1/16·15/16) ≈ 0.24, rounded up), so one count moves a standardized input by at most 1/0.25 = 4 units. Change `Standardizer.fit` to `scale=np.where(std > MIN_SPREAD, std, np.where(std > 1e-9, MIN_SPREAD, 1.0))`: a varying feature keeps its own spread above the floor, a rare one gets `MIN_SPREAD`, a constant one keeps 1.0 as today.
2. `training/ml/jackioh_ml/fit.py`: add `def feature_pulls(float_weights: dict, positions: D.Positions, rows: np.ndarray) -> dict[str, float]`. Inside, build `net = Q.unpacked(Q.quantize(float_weights))` (top-level `from . import export as E` and `from . import quantize as Q`; neither imports `fit`, so no cycle). Precompute each row's `dense` int list and `sparse` key/count list once, plus its base `Q.correction`. For each dense index `j`, perturb a copy with `+1`, take the median over `rows` of `(c1 - c0) * handUnit / handA` (`handA == 0.0` gives 0.0, mirroring `points`). Return `{name: pull}` in `positions.dense_names` order.
3. Same file, `run`: after the seeds loop, `save(best_model, "model.pt")` first (hoist that one call above the report writes; leave the seed and `model-b` saves where they are), then `float_weights = E.from_model(out / "model.pt")` and `pulls = feature_pulls(float_weights, positions, valid_rows)` (the early-stopping validation rows; if empty, all pulls 0.0). Set `report["pulls"] = pulls` and `report["largestPull"] = {"feature": f, "points": p}` for the max by `abs`, ties broken by `dense_names` order. `report.json` then carries both automatically.
4. Same file, `render`: add a `## Feature pulls` section after the learning-curve table: one line defining a pull (median points for one more count over the validation rows, full correction, integer network), then a `| feature | pull |` table of the ten largest by size (`+1` decimal), ties by name.
5. `training/ml/retrain.sh`: at the fit stop (line 118) and tests stop (line 148), read the pull with `python3 -c` from `$out/fit/report.json` into `$pull` and write `{"stage":..., "gain":..., "screened":false, "largestPull":$pull}`. In the screen-stage heredoc (line 177), load `fit_report` the same way and add `"largestPull": fit_report["largestPull"]` to `summary`. All three stages reuse the fit's table (the seeds' nets are alike in strength; the fit's best-validation net is the run's record).
6. `training/ml/tests/test_data.py`: add `test_standardizer_floors_rare_features_at_min_spread`. Build a small dense array: feature A with one 1 in 10,000 rows (spread ≈ 0.01), feature B alternating 0/1 (spread 0.5), feature C constant. Assert `scale[A] == D.MIN_SPREAD`, `scale[B] ≈ 0.5`, `scale[C] == 1.0`, `D.MIN_SPREAD == 0.25`, and that standardizing the lone 1 gives about 4 units. It fails on today's `1e-9` floor (`scale[A] ≈ 0.01`).
7. `training/ml/tests/test_fit.py`: add `test_report_lists_every_dense_features_pull`. Run `F.run` on the fixture with `seeds=(1,)`, `curve=()`; assert `report["pulls"]` has exactly the fixture's dense names with finite values, `report.json` matches, `report.md` holds the `## Feature pulls` table with ten rows, and one feature's pull equals a hand-rolled median from `export.from_model` plus `quantize` over `F._validation_split` rows within 1e-9.
8. Docs, briefly: `training/ml/README.md` fit section (floor value and reason in one line; `pulls`/`largestPull` keys and the top-ten section in two); `docs/learned-eval.md` D5 (standardized inputs floored at `MIN_SPREAD`) and D7 (the pull table is read from the integer network at full correction); `training/learn.md` step 3 (the fit's report and `summary.json` carry the largest pull).
9. Probe printout (not a test): run `/tmp/probe_pulls.py` over the committed `crates/ai/src/learned/weights.json` and the 284 fixture rows mapped into the weights' `denseNames` order by name (missing names 0), perturbing one feature at a time with `quantize.unpacked`/`correction` and converting at share 0.5 (`0.5·Δc·U/a`). Quote the resulting table and the pytest output in the final report; the report's pulls are the same medians at full correction (twice these numbers).

## Tests

- `training/ml/tests/test_data.py`, `test_standardizer_floors_rare_features_at_min_spread`: asserts the floor, the kept common spread, and 1.0 for constants.
- `training/ml/tests/test_fit.py`, `test_report_lists_every_dense_features_pull`: asserts the full table, the ten-row `report.md` section, and integer-arithmetic parity on one feature.
- Commands: `uv run --project training/ml pytest training/ml/tests`. If torch's CPU wheel cannot install, run `cd training/ml && python3 -m pytest tests/test_data.py` (numpy only) and state which suite ran.

## Done when

- [ ] `MIN_SPREAD` exists with its reason; rare features get it, common ones keep theirs, constants keep 1.0.
- [ ] Both new tests pass; the data test fails on the old floor.
- [ ] `report.json`/`report.md`/`summary.json` carry pulls as above at fit, tests and screen stages.
- [ ] The quoted probe table reproduces the issue's swings; the quoted pytest output is green.
- [ ] `git status --short -- crates` is empty; no file outside the table changed.

## Risks

- Pulls cost one Python integer forward per validation row per feature (about 16M on a 100k-game export, hours). The naive loop stays because the pull must be the integer arithmetic that ships; the lane's next run measures the wall time, and a follow-up vectorizes only if it strains the 6-hour job.
- The largest pull in `summary.json` comes from the best-validation net even if another seed ships; seed nets are alike in strength, so the run's record stays comparable.
- Torch is required for the fit test; the data test alone proves the floor if the wheel is uninstallable.

## Open questions

None. The floor's value (0.25) is the judgement call the issue asks the builder to take once, not a person.
```
